findings.title: Offering meets receptive facing
findings.claim: The offering's approach toward nearness is met by reception as a separate responsive act; presentation alone cannot mechanically compel acceptance.
findings.mechanism: The q-r-b approach and offering carriers contact the q-b-l reception and non-reception carriers, while the q-t-l threat exposes the violent redirection that follows an unwelcome outcome.
findings.reader_payoff: Acceptance becomes newly perceptible as a relation between what is offered and the disposition that receives it, rather than as an automatic property of the offering.
findings.containment: This does not claim that the material difference between the offerings is known, or that all rejected offerings are morally corrupt; it preserves the ordinary ritual and acceptance senses.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus word coordinates and trusted publication support a bounded claim about the relation between approach and reception; they do not establish why the offerings differed materially.

findings.title: Spoiled metabolism of work
findings.claim: Exploratorily, non-acceptance resembles failed moral metabolism: outward work is presented, but its inward composition makes uptake corruptive or void rather than nourishing.
findings.mechanism: The focus q-r-b offering and q-b-l uptake carriers contact the attributed 5:53 work-corruption and work-result coordinates, transferring the structure of reception failure across domains.
findings.reader_payoff: The accepted/rejected contrast becomes perceptible as a question about what work becomes when received, not only whether it was visibly performed.
findings.containment: This is a cross-domain analogy, not a lexical equivalence: the ordinary offering, acceptance, and work senses remain primary, and the distant harmful-food image is not imported as a literal gloss.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace gives exact focus and context word coordinates and explicitly marks the reading as an outlier analogy; context roots remain attributed.
